What I want now is simple: a community benefit agreement that is legally binding, not advisory. My family has been in this neighborhood for twenty-three years. We are not asking to be consulted. We are asking to be protected. — Marisol Trujillo, 44, Fruitvale

------------------------------------------------------------ Post-Day 45 To the Editor: My son had a mental health crisis in April. We called 911. Two patrol officers showed up. They were professional and they were kind. They were also not trained for what was happening in my living room. OARI's deadline has passed. Twelve responders hired. Dispatch being tested. I don't care about the politics — who voted yes, who voted no, who is still watching. I care that the next family who calls 911 at two in the morning gets someone who knows what a panic attack looks like. The clock ran out. Please finish this. — Dennis Abara, 52, East Oakland
